Hi Marcus / Camila,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team is excited about Redwood's latency profile. We are trying to firm up a procurement request and need a couple of concrete reservation options to present to our infra committee. Topline requirements:
- Initial pilot: 20 concurrent model workers, avg response size ~250 tokens, peak QPS ~18 (30m sustained bursts)
- Latency SLO: p95 < 350ms for API calls
- Production target (after pilot): 10x that throughput within 3 months if results are good

Could you send 2–3 reservation structures that map to: cluster size (GPU count/shape), a minimum guaranteed GPU floor, and a recommended ramp schedule (pilot -> scale -> steady-state)? Also please highlight operational gating items (warmup credits, cache priming, QA windows, any SOC2 evidence). I've attached our requirements spreadsheet.

Goal: have a shortlist and rough TCO for procurement by Sept 10 so they can include it in the Q4 spend request.

Thanks — Jordan

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity options for Zenport pilot (technical sizing notes)

Thanks for the context — dug into the numbers in the sheet. High level technical recommendations (assumes transformer encoder-decoder 7B-ish model or equivalent optimized variant):

1) Sizing tiers (GPU = A100 80GB equiv):
   - Pilot (conservative): 8 GPUs (1 pod of 8) — expected steady-state QPS ~6–8, can handle short bursts to ~18 qps with aggressive batching; good for validating correctness and latency under low concurrency. Min-GPU floor: 4 GPUs reserved for SLA fallback.
   - Mid (recommended for 3-month scale): 24 GPUs (3 pods of 8, auto-balance) — target steady 18 QPS with p95 headroom < 350ms using continuous batching + KV prefix caching. Min-GPU floor: 12 GPUs.
   - Growth (production-ready): 48 GPUs (6 pods of 8) — support 10x pilot throughput, redundancy across AZs. Min-GPU floor: 32 GPUs for guaranteed baseline.

2) Key configuration levers:
   - Batch window: 10–25ms (tune during pilot)
   - KV cache priming: recommend preloading top 5k prompts during onboarding window
   - Quantization: run 8-bit stable path in prod for mid/growth tiers to reduce GPU memory pressure; pilot can run FP16 for parity testing

3) Ramp schedule (proposal):
   - Day 0–30 (Pilot validation): 8 GPUs active; 2 warmup weeks with synthetic traffic to prime caches
   - Day 31–60 (Scale to mid): increase to 24 GPUs; enable autoscaling window for bursts up to +30% capacity; performance regression evaluation at Day 45
   - Day 61–90 (Stabilize): maintain 24–32 GPUs depending on observed QPS; if all gates pass, activate path to growth
   - Day 91+: growth ramp to 48 GPUs in 2 tranches (to limit cold-start effects)

4) Operational gating items:
   - Warmup credits (3 days of zero-cost warm traffic) to reduce cache cold starts
   - Access to SOC2 report and relevant audit logs for procurement (we can provide export links)
   - Onboarding: 5 business days for config and 2–3 days for smoke tests

I'll convert this into a short PDF matrix for pricing to plug into Camila's sheet.

-Karthik
Senior Infra Architect
Redwood Inference

2) Aug 31–Sept 3: SOW + PO exchange; legal review if enterprise terms requested.

- Canary strategy: use traffic-splitting + throttled burst windows; we will coordinate a logging buffer increase with your infra team during scale windows.
- Warmup credits: included in Option A by default; we will flag it on the SOW.
